> mirddes wrote:
> does not seem to violate card text/rules

When posting a rules question, please ask the question in a clearer way.

If your question is if you can play a Giant's Blood on an uncontrolled vampire, the answer is no (see section 1.6.1.4 of the Rulebook):

Targets. If a card is played on another card, or selects or chooses or otherwise targets another card, the target card must be in play (i.e., controlled). Vampires in the torpor region are eligible targets by default, but vampires in the uncontrolled region and contested cards are not.

V:EKN Website Coordinator

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
> mirddes wrote:
> Blood Doll
>
> Master
>
> Put this card on a vampire you control. During his or her master phase, this vampire's controller may move 1 blood from this vampire to his or her pool or from his or her pool to this vampire.
>
> Why would such cards state controlled if such text is redundant as per 1.6.1.4?
>
To stop you putting the card on someone else's vampire. You can play Giant's Blood on any ready vampire (including ones you do not control). So rather than saying "Fill a ready vampire to capacity" the text relies on the Targeting rule to allow you to only target cards in play.

1.6.1.4 Restricts you to targeting cards which are controlled or 'in play' unless there is specific card text. Uncontrolled vampires are not 'in play' and therefore cannot be targeted by a huge number of other cards.

You cannot put discipline cards on uncontrolled vampires due to 1.6.1.4
You cannot play Anachronism on an uncontrolled vampire due to 1.6.1.4
You cannot play Society of Leopold on an uncontrolled vampire due to 1.6.1.4

So you can't choose an uncontrolled vampire for Giant's Blood.
